LO 1Distinguishing WBC disorders

Q1. How do I tell a blast from a mature cell, and lymphoid from myeloid?

Blast

  • Huge nucleus, fine/open chromatin, nucleoli, scant cytoplasm, mitoses
  • TdT+ (lymphoblasts), CD34+
  • → acute leukemia / lymphoblastic lymphoma; days–weeks
  • Blasts in blood → acute leukemia (≥20% in marrow)

Mature cell

  • Small, condensed nucleus, clumped chromatin
  • TdT−
  • → chronic leukemia, indolent lymphoma, MPN; months

Lymphoid

  • Nodes, lymphocytosis, B or T markers (CD19/20 · CD2/3/7)
  • Replace normal cells → cytopenias

Myeloid (MPN)

  • High counts (granulocytes, RBCs, platelets), big spleen
  • Tyrosine kinase mutations (JAK2, BCR-ABL); CD13/33
  • Overproduce → burn out (fibrosis) or blast out (AML)
In-house exam

Mature lymphocyte = condensed small nucleus; blast = huge nucleus, multiple nucleoli, open chromatin. Pancytopenia argues against an MPN.

Memory tool

Lymphoid neoplasms replace (cytopenias, nodes); MPNs overproduce (high counts, big spleen), then burn out (fibrosis) or blast out (AML).

Q2. How do age and tempo narrow the list?

Age

  • 2–5 y: B-ALL (most common childhood cancer)
  • Teens/young adults: T-lymphoblastic, Hodgkin, Burkitt, DLBCL; not indolent NHL or plasma cell disorders
  • 40s–50s: broad; hairy cell (men), CML, PV
  • 60s+: widest list: CLL, mantle, follicular, MDS, MPN, myeloma, metastases

Tempo

  • Days: lymphoblastic or aggressive lymphoma
  • Weeks: building symptoms, e.g., hyperviscosity (PV)
  • Months: indolent: CLL, hairy cell, indolent lymphoma

ApplyLO 1 application question

A1A 4-year-old has bone pain and petechiae; marrow blasts are TdT+, CD10+, CD19+ with t(12;21). Diagnosis and prognosis?
B-ALL, favorable (t(12;21) and hyperdiploidy are good).

MarkerMeansSeen in
TdTImmature lymphoid cell (B or T precursor)ALL / lymphoblastic lymphoma; negative in Burkitt, CLL
CD34Stem/progenitorALL, AML
CD1a, CD2, CD3, CD5, CD7T cell (CD1a = cortical thymocyte)T-LBL / T-ALL

Memory tool

TdT = "Tiny Developing" cells (blasts). CD5+ B cell = CLL or mantle → CLL has the 23. Hairy cell: "11c, 25, 103 make the hairs grow."

In-house exam

CLL = CD19, CD20, CD5, CD23. Hairy cell = CD11c, CD25, CD103 (+ CD20, CD22).

Q3. What do the cytogenetic and molecular findings mean?
FindingEffectDisease
NOTCH1 point mutationActivates a receptor needed for T-cell development → proliferation, survivalT-LBL / T-ALL
Clonal Ig gene rearrangementAll cells share one rearranged Ig gene = monoclonal B cellsAny B-cell neoplasm
Clonal TCR rearrangementMonoclonal T cellsT-cell neoplasms
del(13q), +12, del(11q), del(17p)del(13q) most common, good; del(17p) = TP53, worstCLL
t(11;14)Cyclin D1 next to IgHMantle cell
t(14;18)BCL2 next to IgH → no apoptosisFollicular
t(8;14)MYC next to IgHBurkitt
t(9;22)BCR-ABL tyrosine kinaseCML (some adult B-ALL)
BRAF V600EMAPK activationHairy cell
JAK2 V617FGrowth-factor-independent signalingPV (~95%), ~½ ET and PMF
MYD88 L265PNF-κB activationWaldenström
Trap — "clonal Ig rearrangement" sounds too generic

When the stem is a mature B-cell neoplasm and no listed translocation fits, it's the right answer: proof of a monoclonal B-cell population. TCR rearrangement would mean a T-cell clone.

Step 1

The 14 in a B-cell translocation is the IgH locus (always-on promoter): 8;14 Burkitt MYC · 11;14 Mantle cyclin D1 · 14;18 Follicular BCL2. 9;22 is the myeloid one.

LO 3Building the differential

Q1. What does each symptom point to?
ClueThink
Chest discomfort (teen)Thymus/mediastinal nodes: lymphoblastic, Hodgkin, Burkitt/DLBCL
Fatigue (older adult)Infection · anemia (always find the cause: iron, chronic disease, MDS, MPN, marrow infiltration) · malignancy
Recurrent pneumoniasImmunocompromised: neutropenia/monocytopenia (hairy cell), hypogammaglobulinemia (CLL), marrow failure
Abdominal "dragging"Enlarged organ: spleen (or polycystic kidneys)
Headache + dizzinessHyperviscosity → cerebral hypoperfusion (PV, Waldenström, leukostasis)
Gastric ulcers + high countsMicrovascular ischemia + basophil histamine → acid (PV)
Plethoric to cyanotic face↑ red cell mass, sluggish deoxygenated flow
High yield — reading the stem

Read in layers: clinical → exam → labs → pathology → ancillary. Read the last sentence first (it may ask natural history, a lab or a gene). Note pertinent negatives: no hepatosplenomegaly, clear lungs, afebrile.

Q2. What is the differential for a mediastinal mass and for lymphadenopathy?

Mediastinal mass (adolescent)

  • Anterior: lymphoblastic lymphoma, Hodgkin, germ cell tumors, thymic lesions (less likely)
  • Middle: lymphoma (nodes)
  • Posterior: neurogenic (neuroblastoma, schwannoma)

Nodes

  • Localized: Hodgkin (contiguous spread)
  • Generalized: lymphoblastic, aggressive NHL, CLL/indolent NHL
  • Tender = infection · soft = lymphoma · hard = metastatic carcinoma
Step 1 — 4 T's of anterior mediastinal mass

Thymoma, Teratoma, Thyroid, "Terrible" lymphoma. Teen boy, fast mass → T-LBL; young woman, fibrous bands → nodular sclerosis Hodgkin.

Q3. What causes splenomegaly, and how do CBC clues sort it?

Splenomegaly

  • Congestive: cirrhosis, portal hypertension
  • Infection: EBV, malaria
  • Hemolysis: spherocytosis, thalassemia, AIHA
  • Malignancy: MPN (CML, myelofibrosis, PV), Hodgkin, NHL (indolent, hairy cell, CLL)

CBC / smear clues

  • Mature lymphocytosis: viral (varied) vs CLL/mantle (monotonous)
  • Pancytopenia: MDS, hairy cell, metastases, aplastic anemia, B12/folate
  • All lines ↑: MPN, especially PV
  • Large platelets: Bernard-Soulier, ITP, MPN
  • Nucleated RBCs: hypoxia, marrow stress, infiltration/fibrosis, hemolysis
Step 1

Massive spleen + low counts → hairy cell or myelofibrosis (both dry tap). Massive spleen + high counts → CML/MPN.

LO 4Histologic clues

Q1. Which histology points to which diagnosis?
LookDiagnosis
Effaced thymus; fine chromatin, convoluted nuclei, many mitosesT-lymphoblastic lymphoma
Smudge cells; node with proliferation centersCLL/SLL
Hairy projections; fried-egg marrow; dry tapHairy cell
Large platelets, nRBCs; hypercellular marrow → fibrosisPV
Starry skyBurkitt
Back-to-back folliclesFollicular
Owl eyes, fibrous bandsHodgkin (nodular sclerosis)
Auer rodsAML (APL)
Toxic granulation, Döhle bodiesReactive (infection)
Plasmacytoid cells + IgMWaldenström

Normal thymus

  • Lobules + Hassall corpuscles

T-lymphoblastic lymphoma

  • Sheets of blasts efface the thymus

CLL

  • Monotonous small mature lymphocytes

Hairy cell

  • Hair-like projections; TRAP+

Massive spleen

  • Red pulp infiltration (hairy cell)

PV smear

  • Large platelets, nRBCs

Spent phase

  • Teardrops → marrow fibrosis
Trap

Normal thymus has lobules, epithelial cells and Hassall corpuscles. Diffuse effacement by blasts = T-LBL, not thymoma.

LO 5The four worked cases

Strategy: each wrong choice is the right answer to a different vignette. Name that vignette and you've explained why it's wrong here.

Case 1. A 14-year-old boy has 5 days of worsening chest discomfort and generalized nodes. CT: 10-cm anterior mediastinal mass. Biopsy: lymphoid cells with lobulated nuclei, fine chromatin, scant cytoplasm, many mitoses; CD2+, CD7+; NOTCH1 point mutation; curable with chemo. Diagnosis?

Answer: lymphoblastic lymphoma (T cell).

DistractorIts home vignette
BurkittB cell, starry sky, MYC, extranodal
FollicularIndolent B, older, BCL2
Nodular sclerosis HLRS cells CD15/30, fibrous bands
Mantle cellOlder men, CD5, cyclin D1
SLLMature B, older, nodes + marrow
In-house exam

T-LBL/T-ALL: NOTCH1, thymus (anterior mediastinal mass), adolescent males.

Case 2. A 70-year-old man has 6 months of fatigue and non-tender cervical and axillary nodes, no hepatosplenomegaly. Hb 9.5, MCV 90, platelets 120k, WBC 42k of monotonous small mature lymphocytes; CD19+, CD5+, TdT−. Cytogenetic/molecular finding?

Answer: clonal rearrangement of immunoglobulin genes (CLL).

DistractorIts home vignette
Clonal TCR rearrangementT-cell neoplasm
t(8;14) MYCBurkitt
t(9;22) BCR-ABLCML
t(14;18) BCL2Follicular (CD10+, CD5−)
Case 3. A 41-year-old man has had several pneumonias in a year, now vague abdominal pain and a dragging sensation; marked splenomegaly. Hb 8.2, platelets 63k, WBC 2,400; small cells with hair-like projections; sputum grows M. kansasii. Most characteristic lab?

Answer: CD20+ and CD11c+ lymphocytes (hairy cell leukemia).

DistractorIts home vignette
Auer rodsAML
Monoclonal IgMWaldenström
t(9;22)CML (big spleen but high WBC)
Toxic granulationReactive infection
In-house exam

Hairy cell: pancytopenia + big spleen, men; monocytopenia → atypical mycobacteria.

Case 4. A 60-year-old woman has 5 weeks of headache and dizziness, gastric ulcers on a PPI, a plethoric-to-cyanotic face and mild splenomegaly. Hb 21.7, Hct 65%, platelets 400k, WBC 30k; large platelets and nRBCs. Natural history?

Answer: marrow fibrosis with extramedullary hematopoiesis (PV spent phase).

DistractorIts home vignette
Gastric NHLMALT (H. pylori), not an MPN outcome
AL amyloidosisPlasma cell disorders
Spontaneous remissionsPV is progressive; needs treatment
B-ALL transformationMPNs transform to AML, not B-ALL

LO 6The four review diseases

Q1. How do the four diseases compare?
T-LBL / T-ALLCLL / SLLHairy cellPV
CellImmature T (thymus)Mature BMature BMyeloid stem cell
PatientAdolescent boy~70Middle-aged/older man~60
TempoDaysMonths–yearsIndolent, progressiveChronic
WhereAnterior mediastinum, nodesBlood, marrow, nodesSpleen, marrow; no big nodesMarrow, blood, spleen
CountsVariable; blasts if leukemicMature lymphocytosis ± anemiaPancytopenia, monocytopenia↑ Hb/Hct, often ↑ WBC, platelets
MarkersTdT, CD1a, CD2, CD3, CD5, CD7CD19, CD20 (dim), CD5, CD23CD11c, CD25, CD103; TRAPLow EPO
DriverNOTCH1del(13q), +12BRAF V600EJAK2 V617F
Feared outcomeSVC/airway compression; CNS/testis relapseInfections, AIHA, Richter → DLBCLInfectionsThrombosis; spent phase; AML
TreatmentMulti-agent chemo (curative)Watch; BTK inhibitors, venetoclaxCladribinePhlebotomy + aspirin
Memory tool

T-LBL: "Teen, thymus, TdT." CLL: "Old man, smudge cells, 5 & 23." Hairy cell: "Spleen big, counts low, TRAPped, BRAF." PV: "Red face, itchy shower, JAK2."

In-house exam

ALL cytogenetics with good prognosis = hyperdiploidy. MDS losses = monosomy 5, 7. Myeloma: IL-6 from plasma + stromal cells drives it.

Q2. How do I separate CLL from mantle cell lymphoma?
CLLMantle cell
Patient / nodesOlder; diffuseOlder men; diffuse; GI polyposis
BloodMature lymphocytosis, smudge cellsLess common
PhenotypeCD5+, CD23+CD5+, CD23−, cyclin D1+
Geneticsdel(13q), +12; Ig rearrangementt(11;14)
NodeDiffuse + proliferation centersVaguely nodular, no proliferation centers
Step 1

CLL = most common adult leukemia in the West; del(13q) most common, del(17p)/TP53 worst. Hairy cell → cladribine (excellent response). PV → thrombosis is the main killer.

ApplyLO 6 application questions

A1A man with PV for 12 years now has a growing spleen, falling hemoglobin, teardrop cells and a dry tap. What happened?
Spent phase: myelofibrosis with extramedullary hematopoiesis.
A2A 75-year-old with CLL develops a sudden fast-growing neck node and fevers. Diagnosis?
Richter transformation to DLBCL.

Sheets of blasts → T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (NOTCH1).

MCQExam-style questions

Score: 0 / 0

1A 15-year-old boy has 1 week of dyspnea and facial swelling. CT shows a large anterior mediastinal mass. Biopsy shows sheets of blasts that are TdT+, CD1a+, CD7+. Which mutation is most likely?

T-LBL; SVC compression.

2A 68-year-old has lymphocytosis of small mature B cells that are CD5+. Which additional marker distinguishes CLL from mantle cell lymphoma?

Mantle: CD23−, cyclin D1+.

3In a patient with CLL, which cytogenetic finding carries the worst prognosis?

TP53 loss.

4A 52-year-old man has massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia and recurrent atypical mycobacterial infections. Marrow aspiration is a dry tap. Best treatment?

Hairy cell leukemia (BRAF; CD11c/25/103).

5A 62-year-old has Hct 60%, WBC 18k, platelets 650k, splenomegaly and pruritus after hot showers. Expected serum EPO and mutation?

PV raises all lines; EPO suppressed.

6A smoker with COPD has Hct 58%, O₂ saturation 86% and high EPO. Platelets, WBC and spleen are normal. Diagnosis?

↑ EPO + ↓ O₂ sat; only RBCs raised.

7A 70-year-old man has mature lymphocytosis (CD19+, CD5+, TdT−) and generalized non-tender nodes. Which molecular finding is expected?

Monoclonal B cells (CLL).

8A patient with a myeloproliferative neoplasm is most likely to transform to which disease?

MPNs blast out to AML or burn out to fibrosis.

9Which feature argues most strongly against a myeloproliferative neoplasm?

MPNs overproduce; pancytopenia suggests hairy cell, MDS, aplastic anemia or marrow infiltration.

10A fast-growing abdominal lymphoma in a 12-year-old is TdT-negative, CD10+, CD20+, IgM+. Which is most likely?

Fast + TdT− = mature aggressive B lymphoma.

11A 60-year-old with polycythemia vera has gastric ulcers. What best explains them?

Hyperviscosity + basophil histamine → acid.

12Which childhood ALL cytogenetic finding is favorable?

Hyperdiploidy and t(12;21) are good.
